headline: Google automatically labels AI-generated ads on Search, YouTube
summary: Google will now automatically flag ads created or edited with its own AI tools, with labels appearing in "My Ad Center" and potentially directly on ads.
details: Google announced it will begin automatically applying a "created or edited with AI" label to ads generated by its proprietary AI tools. This new feature aims to increase transparency for users regarding the origin of advertising content.

The AI label will be visible within Google's "My Ad Center" under the "how this ad was made" section. Users can access this information by tapping the three dots or info icon on any ad across Google Search, Google Discover, and YouTube.

While Google's own AI-generated ads will receive automatic labeling, ads created with third-party AI tools will require manual disclosure from advertisers. In some regions, these labels may also appear directly on the ad itself.

This move aligns with industry trends towards greater transparency in AI-generated content. Meta, for instance, has a similar "AI info" label for ads on its platforms, and Google itself has previously introduced disclosures for "synthetic or digitally altered content" in political ads.
